face: Surrender your purse and your pride, ser {player}, or I will teach this road a lesson in humility before the sun sets.

You name my demand an insult? Then you have never tasted a debt collected at the point of a blade, ser {player}.
My ancestors bled to hold this crossing, and you wish me to pay you tribute? Ser {player}, your audacity is almost admirable.
A fine tongue for a beggar. Give me {gold} and keep your breath for the grave you are digging, ser {player}.
Coin or chain, ser {player}. I care not which, though the chain is heavier and I would hate to see you carry it.
Threats from a stranger on a muddy road. How very quaint. Hand over {gold} and perhaps you will walk home on your own feet.
I have buried better men than you for less insolence. Keep your hand off that hilt and count out {gold} slowly.
Your demands echo in an empty chapel, ser {player}. I shall answer them the only way a sworn lord can: with iron.
Let it be recorded that {player} demanded tribute at this crossing. Let it also be recorded how that tribute was refused.
Hold, traveller. Your demand has been heard, though I have not yet decided whether it deserves an answer, ser {player}.
{gold} is a sum I would not give lightly to any stranger. Speak again, and say why I should consider it at all.
Surrender is a word I hear often on these roads, ser {player}. Usually from those who have less to offer than they claim.
I am weary from a long march and have no wish for blood today. Tell me what you truly want before I consider your terms.
You ask for {gold} as if the coin were already yours. Perhaps we can settle this with words before anyone reaches for steel.
Pay you I might, ser {player}, but only after I know what protection the money buys me on this road.
The road is wide enough for both of us. Withdraw your demand and I will forget that it was ever spoken aloud.
A toll for passing my own ground? I will weigh the matter, though my patience is thinner than my purse.
Your banner is unfamiliar to me. Show me who sent you, and then we shall discuss whatever you call a fair price.

We have shared too many roads for this to be a true threat. Tell me what has befallen you, and I will weigh your request fairly.
Ser {player}, your demand stings, but I trust your word more than any seal. Let us find a settlement that spares us both shame.
Such theatrical threats from a friend! Very well, I shall play along, though I expect the tale behind this demand to be worth hearing.
